items.title: Schuller Gunther — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I remember I looked at George Russell, and we all – I was conducting – we just looked at each other in amazement.

ctx.x: Right. Bill was into that. This piece required that we all should – whether it was Art Farmer, whoever – we should try to deal with Russell’s concept, this theoretical concept. So he’s playing mostly chordal things. Then at the actual recording date, which was two days after the last rehearsal, we started playing that. When his solo came, he burst into this single-note – almost no left hand. Occasionally a chord there – this rattling, driving, energetic, incredibly articulated, fast eighth-note. It veered off and…

items.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I met Gunther at John Lewis’s 20 years before that. Our association wasn’t proven until ’69. He did send a telegram.

ctx.x: One of – I’ve heard from several different sources, and I’ve read also as well, that it was newly formed. I’ve never seen any specific dates, but it was newly formed, and Gunther Schuller wanted you to be a part of it. Of course you and he had an association that went back 20 years before that, at least.
I met Gunther at John Lewis’s 20 years before that. Our association wasn’t proven until ’69. He did send a telegram. It was my time to return to America.
Were you still married at this point, when you returned to America?
